text:
alejandra: Heads-up — VeridianBank POC tomorrow at 11am. They want to demo a tool-calling flow where the model issues a callback webhook to their internal service. Right now callbacks are failing behind their firewall. Need quick presales guidance and a pricing note for dedicated test window.

devin: what's the failure mode? 502? connection reset?

alejandra: connection reset after TLS handshake. Their infra team says corporate firewall only allows outbound TLS to known IPs and inspects SSP. They asked if we support ephemeral inbound webhooks or long-polling pollback.

kai: two immediate options: 1) use webhook callback but run a small NATed reverse-proxy in their VPC (we provide a lightweight container image), or 2) switch the flow to SDK-driven pollback: model emits a function_call with a call_id and we poll our hosted API for call results (pull model). Polling avoids inbound connections.

devin: is the pollback pattern supported in our SDKs? any latency implications?

kai: yes — both Node and Python SDKs have a call-poll helper. Latency depends on polling frequency. For demo-level load (~1-2 concurrent calls) polling at 500ms is fine. For scale, Dedicated or Private is recommended.

lena: security: if we run a reverse-proxy in their VPC, we need their network team to permit egress to our control-plane IPs and to accept mutual TLS with client certs. We'll also want ephemeral creds (short-lived JWTs) for the callback registration so we don't leave long-lived secrets in their config.

alejandra: customer asked if we can do short-lived tokens out of the box.

kai: hosted supports ephemeral API keys via our token broker for enterprise customers (default TTL 15m). We can mint a callback token that expires and rotate on reconnect. SDK helper will handle refresh.

deploy-bot: note: ephemeral-token feature enabled for org: veridian-corp in sandbox.

lena: add to questionnaire: confirm whether their IDS/IPS rewrites headers or strips Authorization on inbound requests. Some appliances drop non-standard headers. Also ask vendor & firmware version.

devin: pricing question: they want a 2-hour dedicated test window for the demo with 10 concurrent streams and occasional function callbacks. Rough cost estimate?

kai: for a short Dedicated window we can offer a transient reservation: 2 x GPU nodes for 2 hours. Rough math: node list-hour rate * 2 nodes * 2 hours. For hosted, cost is usage-based — but with many concurrent streams you risk rate limits and noisy neighbors. For POC, I recommend transient Dedicated to guarantee throughput and avoid firewall retries.

alejandra: can you put numbers? they asked for ballpark now.

kai: ballpark: $3.50 per node-hour for our 1xA100 equivalent pool (PDV). So 2 nodes * 2 hours * $3.50 = $14. We'll draft formal quote. (This is a POC transient discount bucket — enterprise sales to confirm.)

lena: compliance note: if callbacks carry PHI, they need an HIPAA addendum. We should flag legal.

devin: next steps checklist: 1) ask Veridian infra for firewall vendor & firmware, confirm websocket+inbound header handling; 2) offer pollback SDK snippet as fallback; 3) offer reverse-proxy container + instructions if they want inbound; 4) propose transient Dedicated window estimate and confirm billing owner; 5) prepare security questionnaire updates for ephemeral tokens and mTLS.

kai: I'll drop a minimal pollback example for Node now:

```js
// pollback-helper.js (Node SDK)
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.POC_TOKEN });
async function waitForCall(callId){
  while(true){
    const resp = await client.getFunctionCallResult(callId);
    if(resp.status === 'ready') return resp.result;
    await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 500));
  }
}
```

alejandra: perfect. I'll send that to Veridian with the transient Dedicated estimate and ask for vendor info.

devin: I'll also prepare the reverse-proxy README and small container image link so infra can vet it quickly.

lena: I'll update the security questionnaire: add a checkbox for "Will any middleboxes inspect or modify TLS payloads or headers?" and a field for firewall vendor + firmware.

alejandra: thanks everyone. If Veridian signs off on the transient Dedicated we'll need billing contact and PO before we spin nodes up.

deploy-bot: scheduled sandbox resources will be available on approval.

alejandra: ok i'll follow up with Veridian now. :rocket:
